title.narrative: Gemensamt FN Program Ending Violence phase II
UN Joint Programme Ending Violence phase II

description.narrative: Detta är ett fortsatt samarbete med UN för ett gemensamt program/JP för att stoppa våld mot kvinnor. UN Women är det ledande organet och UNDP och UNFPA deltar. JP EVaW fokuserar på tre av de fyra pelarna i Istanbulkonventionen: 1) Förhindra alla former av våld mot kvinnor; 2) Säkerställa effektivt skydd och tillhandahållande av lämpliga tjänster för överlevande; 3) Stödja utvecklingen och genomförandet av en effektiv och integrerad politik för våld mot kvinnor. Programmet riktar sig till alla kvinnor och flickor som har utsatts för våld. Särskilt fokus läggs på kvinnor och flickor som utsätts för diskriminering på flera grunder och intersektionella former. Dessutom engagerar projektet män och pojkar som centrala förändringsagenter för att främja jämställdhet mellan könen. UN-organen har ett nära samarbete med nationella partner, bland annat ministeriet för hälsa och socialt skydd, justitieministeriet, ungdomsministeriet, utbildningsministeriet, inrikesministeriet, den statliga polisen, lokala myndigheter, nationella människorättsinstitutioner, medier, det civila samhället och gräsrotsorganisationer.

This is a continued cooperation with UN for a Joint Programme/JP on ending violence against women. UN Women is the lead agency and UNDP and UNFPA are participating ones. The JP EVaW focuses on three of the four pillars of the Istanbul Convention: 1) Prevent of all forms of VAW; 2) Ensure effective protection and provision of adequate services for survivors; 3) Support the development and implementation of effective and integrated policies on VAW. The programme targets all women and girls who have experienced violence. It places a particular focus on women and girls who are subjected to multiple and intersecting forms of discrimination. Furthermore, the project engages men and boys as pivotal agents of change in the advancement of gender equality. The UN Agencies collaborate closely with national partners, including the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Youth, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of the Interior, the State Police, Local Government Units, National Human Rights Institutions, the media, civil society and grassroots organisations, amongst others.

Project outcomes: 1.Women and girls enjoy more effective preventive measures against violence in Albania. 2.All women survivors and those at risk are better protected from all forms of violence and have equitable access to services in Albania. 3.Responsible institutions and actors implement national policies and legislation on VAW in a more comprehensive, inclusive and coordinated way in Albania.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
The intervention has contributed during 2023 to a stronger institutional commitment to implement laws and policies to address violence against women and better align them with international standards. The UN Joint programme on Ending Violence against Women/EVAW supported the engagement of the Government and of partner CSOs with human rights mechanisms such as the CEDAW Committee and GREVIO. Notably, the recently issued CEDAW Committees Concluding Observations include several important recommendations pertaining to EVAW that were fully or partially aligned with the inputs provided by CSOs and other programme partners, such as the need to urgently amend the definition of rape in the Criminal Code in line with the Istanbul Convention. This and other recommendations were the result of sustained advocacy efforts by UN and partners and will ensure that any upcoming update to the legal and policy framework on EVAW will be more aligned with international standards. Efforts were initiated to establish a Femicide Watch in Albania, providing technical support to the Ombudsperson.
Examples of results include the following:
- Over 1,100 men and boys were involved in awareness raising efforts to combat gender-based violence, including through the strengthening of the Be a Man Club initiative. Faith Based organizations increased their commitment to contribute to the functionality of the CRM and signed formal agreements in Vlora and Pogradec municipalities.
- Overall, UN increased the visibility of messages around EVAW: during the 16 Days Campaign to End Gender Based Violence, UN amplified key messages about prevention and response to GBV and reached over 218,000 people on social media and over 2,400 people through in-person activities, featuring around 180 events (of which at least 61 conducted in the framework of the UN Joint Programme). At least 11 media reports were published on violence against women following UN support, and at least 38 private sector companies joined the campaign through financial or in-kind contributions.
- UN supported the institutional response to ending violence against women and girls. In 2023, 621 cases were reported on the REVALB system, which represents an increase from 2022 (550 cases).
- Considerable support has been provided to strengthening the capacities of the Coordinated Referral Mechanisms (CRMs), ensuring a more cohesive and effective approach to respond and address cases, including strengthening capacities of CRM members in 26 municipalities of Albania such as health professionals, education professionals, police officers, local DV coordinators and municipalities staff.
- The third analysis of the functioning of the CRM at the local level was initiated in 2023 to examine progress, identify best practices and ultimately providing recommendations to overcome the challenges that the CRMs face, and the findings will provide useful for identifying the key priorities for the project for the second year of implementation.
- Some 477 people, mostly women and girls, received services through the intervention including legal aid, psychological support, and reintegration services in 29 municipalities, including at least 31 Roma and Egyptian women, 16 women with disabilities, and 148 women from rural areas. Support to the survivors has been provided by the 16 CSOs engaged through the project, and in coordination with Local Government Units, which play an essential role in identifying and addressing cases of violence as well as raising awareness about VAW.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
